task: Determine VLAN 10’s root and this switch’s interface roles and states. Display the spanning-tree view for that VLAN.

teaching.hint: Choose the instance whose traffic you are investigating.
teaching.takeaway: Compare Root ID with Bridge ID, then read root cost and roles/states together. A healthy alternate port can be discarding; that is not an administrative shutdown.

task: Before calculating a topology, display the switch’s spanning-tree mode and global feature defaults.

teaching.hint: Use the spanning-tree summary rather than an individual VLAN’s port table.
teaching.takeaway: Confirm the actual operating mode. Do not infer it from the switch model or assume a configured edge default proves every interface is operationally an edge.

task: The design requires Rapid PVST+ on this switch. Select that spanning-tree mode.

teaching.takeaway: Verify the operational mode afterward. Rapid PVST+ maintains a separate rapid spanning-tree instance for each VLAN; enabling it does not by itself select your intended root.

task: The lab design selects SW2 as VLAN 10’s preferred root. Apply the root-primary macro for that VLAN.

teaching.hint: Choose the per-VLAN root preference, not an interface role.
teaching.takeaway: The macro sets a bridge priority based on the current root. It does not reserve the role permanently; verify the resulting Root ID and local priority.

task: VLAN 10’s primary uses priority 24576 and other switches use 32768. Apply the root-secondary macro on SW3 for the intended backup preference.

teaching.hint: Choose the secondary root macro for the same VLAN.
teaching.takeaway: The macro sets priority 28672. That is the desired order under these priorities, not a guarantee of second place against every future switch.

task: Set SW1’s configurable bridge priority for VLAN 20 to the lowest legal value above zero.

teaching.hint: Configurable bridge priority changes in blocks of 4096.
teaching.takeaway: Use 4096, not the displayed priority including the VLAN ID. Within one VLAN, priority is compared before the bridge MAC address.

task: On the selected interface, set the local receiving path cost for VLAN 10 to 8 as specified by the topology plan.

teaching.hint: This is a per-interface, per-VLAN cost override.
teaching.takeaway: The value changes STP’s path comparison, not the interface’s physical speed. Recalculate the total root cost and inspect the new role before calling the path correct.

task: The VLAN summary does not explain Gi0/1’s BPDU activity. Display detailed spanning-tree information for that interface.

teaching.hint: Narrow the STP display to the interface and request detail.
teaching.takeaway: Inspect the role, designated information and sent/received BPDU counters in their VLAN context. Counters need a time comparison to show current activity.
